prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on exactly what you need (ACA individual plan vs short‑term vs small‑group options, in‑person help vs online, price vs provider network). I can help, but first a few quick questions:
- Are you looking for an individual/Marketplace (ACA) plan, a short‑term plan, or a small‑business/sole‑proprietor group option?
- Do you prefer a local, in‑person broker or are you okay with an online broker/agent?
- What KC ZIP or neighborhood are you in (so I can find local options)?

If you want to move forward on your own, here are reliable ways to find a high‑quality broker in Kansas City, MO and what to look for:

Where to find licensed brokers
- HealthCare.gov “Find Local Help” (enter ZIP) — lists certified agents and navigators who can enroll you in Marketplace plans and assess subsidy eligibility.
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — use their agent license lookup to confirm a broker’s license status and any complaints.
- National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) local chapter — for experienced, professional brokers.
- Online broker marketplaces (if you prefer remote help): HealthSherpa and eHealth both handle ACA enrollments and compare carriers.

How to choose the right broker (questions to ask)
- Are you licensed in Missouri? (verify with the DOI)
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent (access to many carriers) or captive to one insurer?
- How are you paid? (most brokers are paid by the insurer but ask if they charge any client fees)
- Do you have experience helping self‑employed people get ACA subsidies and use HSAs/QSEHRAs/ICHRA?
- Can you show references or reviews from other self‑employed clients?
- Will you help year‑round (claims/renewals) or only at enrollment?
- Do you help with tax‑related questions like estimating income for subsidy eligibility?

Quick recommendations by scenario
- If you want in‑person local help and personalized planning: use HealthCare.gov’s local agent search or NAHU to find an independent Kansas City broker, then vet them with the questions above.
- If you want fast online comparison and enrollment: HealthSherpa or eHealth are good starting points; you can still request live agent help through them.
- If you’re exploring employer‑style options for a sole proprietor (QSEHRA/ICHRA): look for a broker who explicitly lists small‑employer/HRA experience.

If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you want in‑person help or an online option, I’ll pull up several licensed Kansas City brokers (names, websites, and short notes) you can contact.
